title: Films similar to James Benning’s California Trilogy and non-narrative series & thoughts on reading books to art films

commenti.body:
One that I come back to often is Nikolaus Geyrhalter's *Homo Sapiens*. Observing the liminal remnants of human civilisation through abandoned spaces is sombering to say the least. You could check his other films out. They have a critical tendency towards the impact of humanity on the environment.

Another is Tsai Ming-liang's *Walker* series. Although each entry is brief, the series as a whole is deeply meditative. Another film I would recommend from Tsai Ming-liang is *Stray Dogs*. The second half of the film takes place in an abandoned building, and ends with an arresting 20-minute long shot/reverse shot.

Abbas Kiarostami's *24 Frames* also consists of photographic vignettes lasting around four minutes each. It might please you.

I tend to pair these films with writing, reading or drawing. I also like to put them on in the background when I'm having a long conversation on the phone with a friend. I think it's lovely to mix mediums as you said. Interesting ideas tend to emerge this way.

If I find it to be too long or not engaging enough I'll skip around a little bit. For example watching Peter Hutton's *At Sea* I found some of the scenes of the boat sailing monotonous, so after I'd sat with them for a while I fast forwarded a little. If I'm engaging with a piece of art I want to give it my full attention, and if not I want to go do something else.

Came here to recommend *24 Frames* as well. It's such a relaxing film, and I find it's grown on me over time and a couple rewatches. *Stray Dogs* is in my stack of blu-rays to watch; Tsai Ming-liang is great, so I'll have to get to it (and follow it up with *Days*) soon.

I didnt find 24 frames particularly interesting or well done. The use of animals is the only tool that he utilizes to bring life to the shots and its in literally every frame. Often it feels out of place like the cows by the beach, or the cows in the woods, or the cows in the snow... The concept feels juvenile and something you'd watch for 5 minutes in a museum before forgetting about it forever.

I would recommend Koyaanisqatsi and Baracca or any of the anthropocene style films, theres a few out there

I'm hardly versed in experimental cinema like this but I love Benning. You should check out more of his films. Ruhr is one of the most engrossing films I've ever seen (of course, only if you pay full attention). Same for Stemple Pass.

In the recent film, Saltburn, there's a scene where the main character fucks the grave of another character. It's a 2.5 minute stationary shot of him disrobing and then fucking the dirt. It's very erotic and fun and there's not need to "pair" other artforms, like reading a book. I think watching the character pull out his penis and fuck the grave is stimulating enough without bringing in the latest James Paterson novel, but you do you, boo.
